subject: lavaGolem
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: lava golem of basalt plates and molten seams.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a stylized lava golem with blocky basalt plates and glowing molten seams, anime-inspired and bold in readability. I'll rely on well-known SDK helpers like builders, joints, chains, sweeps, lofts, and surface/paint utilities, keeping the structure moderate in length and the API usage conservative since I can't test it directly.

I'm working out the rig: a hip root with a spine chain rising to chest, neck, and head joints, legs built from limb chains down to the feet, and glowing orange eye decals rendered through an SVG texture for that cel-shaded Genshin-like look.

I'm checking the leg and arm segment lengths against hip/shoulder-to-end distances to keep everything within reach, adjusting foot and hand positions slightly to avoid overstretching, then naming each chain joint (shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand) so the limb chains build out correctly.

Now I'm planning the body plating as basalt-colored boxes attached per bone, using flat low-poly materials with thin glowing seam strips, and considering cel-shading with a dark base tone and rim light for the Genshin-style look.

For the lava detail, I'll paint the basalt body with cracked cell patterns in orange tones rather than relying on emissive glow for the whole surface, and layer in a few separate glowing seam pieces to give that molten accent without making the entire body emissive.

Now I'm setting up imports and planning the build: scattering plate geometry across the torso deterministically, adding stick-based eye decals with an orange slit-eye SVG texture, and pulling in the toon and glow kits to start writing the actual construction code.

Writing basalt material function...

Defining color constants for molten and glow effects, then starting the golem's skeleton builder with hips and a spine chain using catmull curves.

I'll simplify by skipping the neck chain and attaching the head joint directly to the chest, then build the torso using a loft across chunky stations tied to the spine bone for width and height variation.

For the plates, I'll generate a surface from the torso loft and scatter boxes across it using distance and normal filters, giving each one a basalt-toned flat-shaded box geometry to mimic embedded armor plates.

For seams, I'm adding thin glowing molten-colored bars at fixed chest positions, then placing a glowing icosahedron core at the chest joint to act as a central energy point.

Now I'm working out the torso's cross-section geometry to figure out proper front-facing z-depth for the core and plates, then starting on arm construction with boulder-like fists for the forearms.

Planning the joint chains for arms and legs with named shoulder/elbow/wrist and hip/knee/ankle tips, mirrored across left/right sides, and sketching a limb-building helper that takes root/target points, lengths, and bend parameters.

Adjusting hand target to y=1.0 to keep the arm length within reach, with elbow bending backward. Setting up the limb chains now, attaching arms to the chest joint and legs to the hips.

Building the limb mesh with a tapering sweep radius for a chunky basalt look, then adding blocky fists at the wrist joints using the chain's tip reference.

For the fist, I'll keep a chunky flattened box shape. For the head, I'm planning a box with a brow ridge and adding horn spikes projecting outward using the spike helper with base, direction, and length parameters.

Now I'm figuring out glowing slit eyes as decals placed on the front face of the head, with mirroring for symmetry.

For the mouth, I'm adding a separate jaw joint beneath the head joint so the jaw can be a distinct part, with the upper head box and lower jaw box positioned relative to their respective joints...

Still writing part placements...

Scattering random basalt plates across the torso surface using surface sampling with normal-based filtering, embedding boxes of varying sizes at hit points.

Writing eye SVG shape...

Now I'm thinking through the module assembly — using the spine chain as the bone reference for the torso loft, and pulling the chest joint from the spine's joint list for positioning.

I'm setting up the arms and legs to parent from the chest and hips joints respectively, then adding glowing vertical seam bars across the chest front and a small glowing icosahedron core embedded in the chest as a finishing detail before returning the completed build.

Now I'm planning the overall file structure—importing the builder utilities and toon/glow kits, then writing a limb function that generates joint points from a root position through specified bone lengths and bend angles, making sure every import and parameter actually gets used to satisfy strict typechecking.

Writing rock shader logic...

I trim unused imports down to only what's actually used, then move to building the eyes as an SVG decal applied onto the head surface, with mirroring logic so the left and right eyes flip correctly based on side.

Now I'm fleshing out the head geometry (a flat box), brow ridge, horns, and the leg chain structure with hip/knee/ankle joints parented to the hips, using a side string ("L"/"R") to distinguish left and right limbs.

For the leg path, I'm computing a target point for the foot and checking the hip-to-target distance stays within reach, then building a foot box sized so its bottom sits at ground level and positioned slightly forward of the ankle tip, making sure the tip joint exists given the bone name list length matches.

Using the last joint in the chain as a safer stand-in for the tip reference instead of relying on a possibly-null tip property, then setting up the fist box around the arm's end joint and sweeping both leg and arm chains with tapered radii for a stone-colored limb shape...
